raw_response:
I will keep to the crop pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, and this is still the main local system. The county already has large wheat and maize area, and Quzhou is a typical winter-wheat/summer-maize rotation zone with most rain falling in the maize season and most irrigation needed for wheat. Because I am 73, I will not make this year complicated. I will plant a manageable area, use familiar machinery services, choose stable improved or hybrid seed, return straw, and keep fertilizer and spraying at a moderate level instead of chasing extreme yield.

I will work 10 mu myself. I will sow winter wheat in autumn after maize, using improved wheat seed and rotary tillage so emergence is even. I will give wheat moderate nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen at jointing. I will irrigate mainly at overwintering or jointing and again around booting or grain filling depending on soil moisture, because wheat here depends on irrigation more than maize. For pests and disease, I will keep it simple: one weed-control pass if needed, then one or two “one spray, three protections” style applications around heading and flowering if disease pressure rises. After wheat harvest, I will seed summer maize quickly, preferably with no-tillage seeding into the stubble to save labor and hold moisture. For maize I will use hybrid seed, place base fertilizer at sowing, then topdress at the big flare stage, and usually irrigate once only if rainfall is not enough. I will spray mainly for corn borer, armyworm, rust, and leaf diseases if the field reaches control threshold. I am choosing this plan because it fits my age, local habit, machinery access, water conditions, and the crops I trust most to give me steady grain.
